title: Shared folder permissions wrong
symptom: User cannot open a team folder on the file server they should have access to
user_description: I moved to the Key Accounts team last week but I still can't open their folder on the shared drive. My manager already said yes by email. Can you just give me access?

options.text: Give Everyone full control of the folder
options.why: Lets every user change or delete the team's files. Far too much access.

options.text: Add him to the folder directly with full control
options.why: Individual permissions are hard to manage, and full control is more than he needs.

options.text: With the owner's approval, add him to the team's security group with the least access needed, and check both the share and NTFS permissions
options.why: Groups keep access tidy and easy to remove later. When share and NTFS permissions both apply, the stricter one wins, so both must allow access.

options.text: Make him a local administrator on his PC
options.why: Admin rights on his PC do not give access to a folder on the server, and add risk.

hints: Who should approve access to a team's folder?
Is it better to give access to a person or to a group?
Which permissions apply on a network folder?
real_world_tip: Keep the manager's approval with the ticket. Group-based access also makes it easy to remove when he moves teams again.
